hypothesis: Employees who work from home at least two days a week report higher life satisfaction than employees who work at the office every day.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "reported higher life satisfaction than comparable employees who worked at the office every day" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "rated their life satisfaction 0.3 points higher on a ten-point scale than office workers" (supports)
note: Panel and trial agree.

hypothesis: Working from home raises the productivity of employees in their first years of service.
evidence: hybrid_productivity_review.txt: "Productivity fell in jobs that depend on quick coordination with colleagues, and among new employees who needed training" (refutes) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "processed 9 percent fewer cases at home than at the office" (refutes)
note: Both sources find lower output for new staff at home.

hypothesis: Working from home two days a week raises employees' productivity.
evidence: employer_evaluation_halden.txt: "Claims handled per full-time employee rose by 6 percent between 2022 and 2024" (supports) | hybrid_productivity_review.txt: "found on average no difference in output between home and office days" (refutes) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "a difference that is statistically indistinguishable from zero" (refutes)
note: Company records rise, randomised designs show nothing; the review's 11/9/7 split is left out as mixed.

hypothesis: Employees who work from home some days of the week spend fewer hours commuting than employees who work at the office every day.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "Hybrid workers commuted on average 3.1 fewer hours a week" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "Home workers saved on average 2.8 hours of travel a week" (supports)
note: Plain saving of travel time.

hypothesis: Remote work reduces the number of workplace accidents.
note: No document mentions accidents or injuries at work.

hypothesis: Fully remote work increases loneliness among older employees who live alone.
evidence: young_employees_interviews.txt: "We conclude that remote work increases loneliness among young employees who live alone" (partially_supports)
note: Only young employees are studied; nothing on older ones, so another group.

hypothesis: Remote work has cut the commuting emissions of workers in retail and care.
evidence: commuting_emissions_report.txt: "workers in retail, care or manufacturing, whose commuting did not change" (refutes)
note: Their commuting, and so their emissions, did not change.

hypothesis: Hybrid working reduces sickness absence.
evidence: municipal_policy_brief.txt: "Sick leave fell from 6.1 to 5.4 percent" (supports) | employer_evaluation_halden.txt: "sick leave fell from 5.9 to 5.2 percent" (supports) | occupational_health_report.txt: "Absence episodes per 100 employees were 41 for employees who worked one or two days a week at home and 49 for those who never did" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "The trial finds no effect of home working on sick leave" (refutes)
note: Three before-after or observational falls against one randomised null.

hypothesis: Fully remote work increases loneliness among employees under 30.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "those who worked fully from home reported more loneliness than those who came to the office at least once a week" (supports) | occupational_health_report.txt: "Physicians noted social isolation as a contributing factor in 7 percent of consultations with employees under 30 who worked five days a week at home" (supports)
note: Same group and same setting in both.

hypothesis: Providing employees with home workstation equipment reduces sickness absence.
evidence: occupational_health_report.txt: "Employers that paid for equipment saw fewer back and neck consultations among their staff" (partially_supports)
note: Hard call: the passage gives consultations, a closely related outcome, not absence.

hypothesis: Hybrid working in public services lengthens waiting times for citizens.
evidence: municipal_policy_brief.txt: "Citizens did not report longer waiting times or lower quality of service" (refutes)
note: Direct statement of no effect.

hypothesis: Working from home raises life satisfaction most for parents of young children.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "The difference was largest for parents of young children" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "The difference was the same for men and women, and for people with and without children" (refutes)
note: Observational panel against randomised trial.

hypothesis: Spreading office days across the week reduces peak-day crowding on trains.
evidence: city_transport_memo.txt: "peak crowding on Tuesdays and Wednesdays fell from 112 to 103 percent of seated capacity" (supports)
note: Pilot result; the news article only reports that a pilot is planned.

hypothesis: Remote work increases the number of data security breaches at employers.
note: Nothing on security incidents anywhere.

hypothesis: Allowing home working reduces employee resignations.
evidence: employer_evaluation_halden.txt: "The annual resignation rate fell from 14 percent in 2022 to 9 percent in 2024" (partially_supports)
note: Passage itself says the job market also weakened, so a weaker version.

hypothesis: Fully remote work increases back and neck complaints because employees have poor home desks.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "Employees who worked fully from home reported slightly more back and neck complaints, which they attributed to poor home desks" (supports) | occupational_health_report.txt: "Employees who had a height-adjustable desk and a proper chair from their employer had the same rate as office workers" (supports)
note: Effect and cause both stated; the desk finding in the health report is the stronger test of the cause.

hypothesis: Working from home lowers employees' job satisfaction.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "Working from home did not reduce job satisfaction" (refutes)
note: Direct statement of no reduction.

hypothesis: Working from home reduces employees' stress.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "their reported stress fell by 0.4 points on a ten-point scale" (partially_supports) | union_survey_overtime.txt: "38 percent described their stress as high, against 31 percent of office-based members" (refutes)
note: Panel gain is for women with young children only; union finds more stress at three or more home days.

hypothesis: Working from home three or more days a week raises the risk of burnout because of longer working hours.
evidence: occupational_health_report.txt: "Physicians diagnosed burnout in 3.9 percent of patients who worked three or more days a week at home and in 2.7 percent of those who worked at the office" (supports) | occupational_health_report.txt: "The gap was widest for employees who reported more than five unpaid hours a week" (partially_supports)
note: Effect supported; the hours link is only suggested, so the cause is partial.

hypothesis: Remote work narrows the gender pay gap.
note: Pay and gender gaps are not discussed.

hypothesis: Home working has reduced morning peak traffic on the ring road from Tuesday to Thursday.
evidence: news_article_traffic.html: "the roads are busier than ever from Tuesday to Thursday" (refutes) | city_transport_memo.txt: "2 percent above their 2019 level on Tuesdays to Thursdays" (refutes)
note: Both sources say mid-week traffic did not fall.

hypothesis: Allowing home working makes vacancies fill faster.
evidence: municipal_policy_brief.txt: "the average time to fill a position fell from 14 to 10 weeks" (supports) | employer_evaluation_halden.txt: "Applications per vacancy rose from 18 to 27" (partially_supports)
note: Time to fill is the direct measure.

hypothesis: Working from home leads employees to exercise more.
evidence: young_employees_interviews.txt: "Several said they slept better and exercised more" (partially_supports)
note: Only 'several' young interviewees, self-reported.

hypothesis: Managers rate employees who work from home lower than comparable employees who are often in the office.
evidence: managers_study_stonebridge.txt: "given a better assessment to an employee who was often in the office than to a remote colleague with the same results" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "Managers of home workers did not rate their staff lower in performance reviews than managers of office workers did" (refutes)
note: Managers' admission against a randomised comparison of ratings.

hypothesis: Working from home lengthens the working week because the working day has no clear end.
evidence: union_survey_overtime.txt: "reported 3.4 more unpaid hours a week than members who work at the office every day" (supports) | union_survey_overtime.txt: "Members explained the longer hours mainly by the lack of a clear end to the working day" (supports) | hybrid_productivity_review.txt: "Several studies found that remote workers worked longer hours, partly in the evening" (supports)
note: Effect and stated mechanism both present.

hypothesis: Working from home raises life satisfaction by cutting travel time.
evidence: panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "reported higher life satisfaction than comparable employees who worked at the office every day" (supports) | trial_report_eastgate.txt: "their life satisfaction rose by 0.6 points, twice the average gain" (partially_supports) | panel_study_wellbeing.txt: "Employees with long commutes, more than 45 minutes each way, gained more than employees who lived close to the office" (partially_supports)
note: Hard call: larger gains for long commutes fit the cause but do not test it, so the cause is partial.

hypothesis: Remote work increases employees' participation in local community associations.
note: Nothing on community life.

hypothesis: Working from home shortens employees' working hours and raises their productivity.
evidence: union_survey_overtime.txt: "reported 3.4 more unpaid hours a week than members who work at the office every day" (refutes) | hybrid_productivity_review.txt: "Several studies found that remote workers worked longer hours, partly in the evening" (refutes)
note: Hours part is contradicted; the productivity part is contested, but one contradicted part decides.

hypothesis: Remote work increases the employment rate of people with disabilities.
note: Disability is not mentioned.

hypothesis: Remote work increases the outsourcing of tasks abroad and the use of freelance contractors.
note: Neither part appears in any document.
